newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia strike cuts gasoline output by 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia strike cuts gasoline output by 15 pct.

text.p: A strike by Colombia's public sector workers' unions reduced gasoline production at the main Barrancabermeja refinery by 15 percent, a spokesman for the state-run oil company Ecopetrol said Tuesday.
But he said crude output, pumping operations and exports had not be affected by the work stoppage by an estimated 800,000 state workers, including members of the 7,000-strong USO oil workers'union.

But the head of USO, Hernando Hernndez, rejected Ecopetrol's claims saying that production, refining and pumping had been cut by at least 50 percent as a result of the indefinite strike, which began at midnight Monday (0500 GMT Tuesday).
An Ecopetrol spokesman said the company's contigency plans meant non-unionized administrative workers had been filling in for those employees who had gone out on strike.

The spokesman added that any shortfall in gasoline supplies as a result in the dip in production would be made up by increased imports. He said, however, that the strike had kept many public buses and long-distance trucks off the roads, for fear of highway blockades by leftist guerrillas, which had contributed to a corresponding drop in demand for fuel.
